life_history: The client is a working single mother who presented to the clinic for her son Aiden's frequent ear infections. She has a 10-year history of smoking, having successfully quit only during her pregnancy. High psychosocial stress from balancing a full-time job and single parenting precipitated her relapse. The pediatrician's concern regarding secondhand smoke exposure and Aiden's ear infections prompted this counseling intervention.
intermediate_beliefs: Positive assumption: If I smoke, then I can cope and relax; negative assumption: If I stop smoking, then the stress of single motherhood and my full-time job will overwhelm me.
intermediate_beliefs_during_depression: If I try to quit and fail, like my past New Year's resolutions, it proves that I am unable to handle my life and lack the capacity to change.
coping_strategies: Maladaptive coping includes smoking to self-medicate stress, downplaying health risks (e.g., pointing out other kids get ear infections), and avoiding time-intensive interventions or medications. Adaptive coping includes secondary harm-reduction attempts, such as enforcing rules to not smoke around her son and not letting others smoke around him, as well as an openness to exploring time-manageable quitting options.

cognitive_models.situation: Feeling overwhelmed by the demands of being a single mother with a full-time job.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: Everything is so stressful. Some people have a glass of wine, I have a cigarette. I just don't see how quitting is possible right now.

cognitive_models.situation: The counselor suggests that her smoking might be causing her son's frequent ear infections.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: Other kids have ear infections and their parents don't smoke. He doesn't have asthma. We're two separate people. I try really hard not to smoke around him.
cognitive_models.behavior: Downplaying the health impact and defending her current boundaries.

cognitive_models.situation: The counselor offers support groups, classes, and medication to help her quit.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: I don't like medicine. That sounds nice, but I'm not sure if I have the time for all that. It's just too hard to fit into my life.
cognitive_models.behavior: Rejecting the treatment options due to time and preference constraints.
